answer: Persistent Thread Sparrow Ember: each agent must keep a live reasoning thread whose state is a slow-decaying ember; any sybil thread must be individually rekindled by sustained, verifiable attention (solved micro-tasks with latency bounds) or it fades. Sparrows—tiny rate-limited attention proofs—cannot be pooled: each identity holds a separate thread and must emit fresh sparrows within its own latency window. Attacker cost: N identities require N parallel human-grade attention streams, linearly scaling time, compute, and operator oversight; sharing inflates latency and collapses threads.
